Approval Basis: Employer assigns fire detection system servicing, maintenance and testing to a trained person knowledgeable in the systems under 8 CCR 6183(c)(4); competence is determined by the employer and no external body approves the training or the trained person.
Frequency: Before performing servicing, maintenance or testing of the system
Notes / Research Flags: Thin obligation — servicing/maintenance/testing of fire detection systems must be performed by a 'trained person'; single undifferentiated requirement. Flagged for reviewer given thinness. | [AUTO] Cross-setting enumeration: Cal/OSHA building and physical-plant hazard duty, 13 settings | [AUTO] Impact basis: Subsection (c)(4) requires the inspection and maintenance to be performed by a trained person knowledgeable in the operations and functions of the system - a restriction on who may perform the task as well as a training duty. (confidence High) | [AUTO] Cross-setting enumeration: Cal/OSHA building and physical-plant hazard duty, 13 settings. Hazard arises from operating a building, its grounds and its service equipment; enumerated across the 13 building-based HSTM settings. Home Health is excluded because its work is performed in the patient's residence, not in an employer-operated plant. | Family: fire protection system trained-person designation (6165, 6175, 6183, 6184) - all four members take the same determination. Self-refutation check: the 'approved' systems, components and installation manner in these sections (and the NFPA references) are equipment and installation approvals, not training approval. Instructor/SME is No: the knowledge requirement attaches to the person performing the inspection or servicing work, not to whoever delivers the training. Cal/OSHA pattern: the employer designs, delivers and where required certifies the training; DOSH enforces by inspection and citation and does not pre-approve training content. | NFPA citation kept in its native form.
Interpretive Conditions: The servicing, maintenance, cleaning, sensitivity adjustment and testing that § 6183(c)(4) reserves to a trained person are performed against the NFPA 72 criteria the Article incorporates, so the knowledge the trained person must hold is defined by that standard; § 6183(e)(2) ties detection systems installed for employee alarm and evacuation to the § 3220 emergency action plan those systems trigger.
Regulatory Change Summary: Servicing, maintenance and testing of fire detection systems must be performed by a trained person knowledgeable in the operations and functions of the systems.
Interpretive Summary: A competence qualification on who may perform the work, with no employer-delivered curriculum stated.
